title: Training Data Attribution: Was Your Model Secretly Trained On Data Created By Mine?

problem.claim: Determine whether a suspicious text-to-image model was trained wholly or partially on data originating from a specific source model.

gap.claim: Existing attribution methods require additional watermarks during source-model training or inference, making them impractical for released pre-trained models whose owners may lack security expertise.

contributions.claim: An injection-free training-data attribution method identifies whether a model's training data stems from a specified source model without adding watermarks to the source model.
Instance-level detection-based and generation-based strategies use distinct samples as inherent watermarks to test whether a suspicious model originates from the source model.
A statistical-level attribution method uses a shadow model to train an attribution discriminator.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report attribution accuracy and AUC scores above 80% even when the infringing model uses only a small proportion of generated data.

narrative_sequence.summary: Text-to-image models raise concerns about potential infringement when generated data is reused without authorization.
Attribution must determine whether suspicious-model training data originated from a specific source model, but existing watermark-based methods are impractical for released pre-trained models.
The proposed approach exploits inherited memorization, combining instance-level strategies with a statistical-level shadow-model discriminator.
Experiments report attribution accuracy and AUC above 80% under limited use of generated data.
